A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December.
In the aftermath of a selloff that roiled Wall Street, the Nasdaq 100 climbed 1.2%. A gauge of chip giants rallied 3%. Software shares fell. Microsoft Corp. was said to be winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle Corp. Treasury two-year yields rose.

It took around 24 hours for Wall Street’s response to the US midterm elections to turn negative. Once it did, it set in motion a chain reaction of selling that moved considerably faster.
The blue wave that swept Congress was initially met with a solid gain in American stocks, with the event risk tied to the vote out of the way and oil prices in retreat, and on expectations the Trump administration would now be reined in. But by Thursday morning, investors were reassessing the wider implications, and the Democrats’ deep skepticism of the data-center expansion on which the artificial intelligence revolution depends.

Global benchmark Brent traded near $98 a barrel, flipping between gains and losses. Prices had retreated after Bloomberg reportedBloomberg Terminal

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Argentine global bonds are heading for their worst week in over a year as a global retreat from risk collides with growing investor anxiety over next year’s presidential election.
The benchmark 2035 note lost more than three cents on the dollar, pushing the yield to 13.77% on Friday from 12.67% at the end of last week. The extra yield investors demand to hold Argentine debt over US bonds widened almost 140 basis points to 928 — more than double its July low — in the first four days of the week, according to a JPMorgan index.

Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government plans to transition up to 200,000 temporary residents to permanent residency by the end of 2027, in addition to its annual immigration target.
The Canadian government’s immigration levels plan maintained its annual targets for temporary and permanent residents at 370,000 and 380,000 respectively through 2029. But a one-time measure will also grant permanent residency to individuals who are already in the country on a temporary basis.

At least two more credit trading pods running money for Millennium Management are leaving the hedge fund giant.
Dominick Maggio and Amit Agrawal, who ran Abacove Capital within Millennium, are leaving, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Mark Meenan and David Ulrich, who managed money at Twin Lights, another internal trading pod of Millennium, are also leaving, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

item.description: A rebound in chipmakers buoyed Wall Street as dip buyers emerged despite solid economic readings that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December. item.title: US Job Growth Surged in October, Unemployment Rate Fell
item.description: US job growth surged in October and the unemployment rate edged lower, a sign of labor-market strength in an expanding economy. Nonfarm payrolls increased 165,000 last month, topping all forecasts, after an upward revision to the prior two months. Claudia Sahm, Chief Economist at New Century Advisors, reacts to the report. (Source: Bloomberg)
